chapter: Leaving Hampton and starting his own band
title: Why he left: monopoly over his outside work and fear for his wife
summary: Cobb explains he left because Hampton and Gladys wanted every booking to come through them, and he took a witness because he feared the notice would be denied.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: So I said, 'Well, you go so far and -- of course, I had saved me some money, and I would go on and form my own band; not form my own band, to play this job, I was forming a band for the two weeks I had in Philadelphia (inaudible). And I was determined mostly to go after I found out that they wanted to block me on it because it didn't come through Gladys and Hamp. Well, I said, well. I said, this is really a monopoly -- people monopolize your life, where you can't make a quarter. They going to make everything on you. Come through me first!
Well, even if you've got to take a witness to hand your notice in, that's pretty sad.
I did it because I was afraid that it might not be recognized because he'd say, 'I never received it.'

That's why I took a witness. See, there's so many little technical things. And when they're like they were, I was afraid of it unless I had somebody there. But all I wanted to do was get out, because, see, I was called in New York. And I told my wife I'd just tell anybody to call me (inaudible). He called me twice, but I

was through then, and I'm through, I'm through. If I have to tell me wife I'm through, I'm through. You don't play games with a situation like that. If you're serious, be serious. But you can't just jump back and forth, back and forth. No good. And people will take advantage of you if you do it, like you need them.
